append.text: **Ps 72:2 *pæne moti sunt pedes* → *quase foram abalados*** — the passive kept; no reader remarked. *vacilaram* (MS1932) option.
**Ps 72:3 *zelávi super iníquos* → *invejei os iníquos*** — applied as the row asked; *super* absorbed by the transitive verb. Passed the Latinist twice, no reader remarked.
**Ps 72:5 *In labóre hóminum* → *na fadiga dos homens*; 72:16 *labor est ante me* → *é fadiga diante de mim*** — one noun twice; the stylist asked the bare *é fadiga* (v2) to echo 72:5.
**Ps 72:7 *Pródiit quasi ex ádipe* → *saiu como que da gordura*** — applied; passed.

**Ps 72:7 *ex ádipe* → *da gordura*** — the image kept; the ambiguity reader heard iniquity oozing like grease, or sin from prosperity (both the Latin's range); the stylist asked the order *Como da gordura saiu*, refused (colon-initial *Como* is 'How' in this psalm).
**Ps 72:8 *locúti sunt nequítiam* → *falaram maldade*** — beside *iniquitátem → iniquidade* in the next colon; passed.

**Ps 72:8, 72:11 *in excélso* → *no alto* (both)** — one wording for the repeated phrase (the Greek differs: εἰς τὸ ὕψος, ἐν τῷ ὑψίστῳ); heard as 'loftily' at 72:8 and 'up above' at 72:11. Passed the Latinist twice.
**Ps 72:11 *Quómodo scit Deus, et si est sciéntia in excélso?* → *Como é que Deus sabe, e se há saber no alto?*** — *scit … sciéntia* → *sabe … saber*, the root kept; 72:21 *nescívi* → *não soube*.

**Ps 72:1 *Quam bonus* → *Como Deus é bom*; 72:19 *Quómodo facti sunt* → *Como se tornaram uma desolação!*; 72:11 interrogative *Quómodo scit Deus* → *Como é que Deus sabe*** — the ambiguity reader heard bare *Como sabe Deus* as an exclamation of God's knowledge; *é que* marks the question.

**Ps 72:12 *abundántes in sǽculo* (εὐθηνοῦντες, of persons) → *prósperos no mundo*** — *abundantes* is heard as 'numerous' with persons; the row's option supplies the adjective. Passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 72:14 *et castigátio mea in matutínis* → *e o meu castigo, nas madrugadas*** — applied as the row asked, verbless as the Latin; heard as 'punished in the early mornings'. Passed the Latinist twice.
**Ps 72:16 *Existimábam ut cognóscerem hoc* → *Eu pensava em conhecer isto*** — applied (D44); passed.
**Ps 72:18 → *Todavia*** — applied.
**Ps 72:18 *propter dolos* → *por causa dos enganos*** — whose deceits left open, as the Latin.
**Ps 72:19 *súbito defecérunt* → *de repente desfaleceram*** — applied.

**Ps 72:19 *súbito defecérunt* (persons, ἐξέλιπον 'came to an end') → *desfaleceram*; 72:26 *Defécit caro mea, et cor meum* → *Desfaleceu*** — one verb kept for the end of the wicked and the psalmist's own failing (the psalm's echo), despite the 11:2 warning about persons; the ambiguity reader listed *desfaleceram* unknown, heard nothing wrong; the Latinist passed it twice. *se acabaram* at 72:19 is the option.
**Ps 72:20 *ad níhilum rédiges* → *reduzireis a nada*; 72:21 *ad níhilum redáctus sum* → *fui reduzido a nada*** — identical in both; *dedúcere me* at 72:24 → *me guiastes* (D22).

**Ps 72:21 *renes mei commutáti sunt* → *os meus rins foram mudados*** — the ambiguity reader heard literal kidneys and listed *rins* unknown; kept (the organ named). *se alteraram* (ἠλλοιώθησαν) is heard as 'got upset'; *se mudaram* as 'moved house'.

**Ps 72:23 singular *Ut juméntum* (κτηνώδης) → *como um jumento*** — a local departure from *animal* in v2, asked by the Latinist and the stylist: one beast of burden, and in Brazil the byword for a dull mind, which is the sense after 72:21 *e não soube*. The plural herds keep *animais*. Gate v2 passed it.
**Ps 72:23 *factus sum apud te* → *junto de vós*** — applied; passed.

**Ps 72:24 *cum glória suscepísti me* → *com glória me acolhestes*** — a person as object but the Greek is προσελάβου ('took me to yourself'; the Palm Sunday Gradual reads *assumpsísti*), so D15's test sends it here, not to D19's *amparar*; MS1932 *acolheste*. Passed the Latinist twice. *amparastes* option.

**Ps 72:27 *qui elóngant se a te* → *os que se põem longe de vós*** — applied; the stylist called it a laboured calque and asked *se afastam* (discédere's verb), kept as option — **for Gustavo**, with 21:20. The Latinist passed it twice.
**Ps 72:27 *períbunt: perdidísti* → *perecerão: fizestes perecer*** — applied as D24 names; the colon runs +6.
**Ps 72:28 *Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est* → *Mas para mim é bom apegar-me a Deus*** — applied as the row names; the versicle read alone; passed every reader.

append.row: | *Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine*
append.text: **Ps 72:13 *et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas* → *e lavei as minhas mãos entre os inocentes*** — copied from 25:6; the ambiguity reader heard Pilate's gesture as a second reading.

terms: | respéctus (*non est respéctus morti eórum*) | respeito a (*não há respeito à morte deles*) | open | Ps 72:4 (ἀνάνευσις, a crux). Whose regard is missing is left open, as the Latin; the ambiguity reader heard 'they do not fear death' first. The stylist asked *respeito para a*, refused; *consideração pela* and MS1932's *temor da* are options. Passed the Latinist twice. |

| firmaméntum (of the wicked: *firmaméntum in plaga eórum*) | firmeza | open | Ps 72:4 (στερέωμα; DRB 'strength'), the local place D31 left: neither *esteio* (God) nor *firmamento* (sky). The colon stays verbless — v1 supplied *há*, which the Latinist ruled a major (it settles whether *non est* carries over). Heard as 'strong even in affliction'. *plaga* → *flagelo* (D39) against the Latinist's *chaga*: the Greek repeats μάστιξ / μαστιγόω in 72:4–5. |

| tenére (*ténuit eos supérbia … Tenuísti manum déxteram meam*) | tomar (*a soberba os tomou … Tomastes a minha mão direita*) | open | Ps 72:6, 72:24: one verb (ἐκράτησεν / ἐκράτησας) for pride seizing the wicked and God holding the psalmist — the psalm's turn. The Latinist asked 'held' three times (*reteve*, *prendeu*, *Segurastes*); held, since his fixes split the pair. *segurar* for both is the option — **for Gustavo**. |

| afféctus (*transiérunt in afféctum cordis*) | aos afetos do coração | open | Ps 72:7 (διάθεσιν); the plural keeps the older sense (movements of the heart), the singular *afeto* is heard as fondness. The Latinist asked the singular twice (option); the ambiguity reader listed *afetos* unknown. *às paixões* (MS1932) option. |

| justificáre cor (*justificávi cor meum*) | tornar justo (*sem causa tornei justo o meu coração*) | open | Ps 72:13 (ἐδικαίωσα). Draft 1's cognate *justifiquei* was heard as 'I made excuses for' by the ambiguity reader; v2 *tornei justo*, passed the gate. *justificar* stays for justificatiónes (the statutes) and for God as subject. |

| nátio (*natiónem filiórum tuórum*) | nação | open | Ps 72:15 (γενεά); *geração* (DRB) is generátio's. Collides only with *gentes → nações*; they do not meet here. *reprobávi* kept indicative → *rejeitei* (the reprobáre row). Passed the Latinist twice. |

| novíssima (*in novíssimis eórum*) | o fim deles | open | Ps 72:17 (τὰ ἔσχατα); DRB, MS1932. The Latinist asked the plural *as últimas coisas deles* twice (option); *os novíssimos* is the catechism's word. Heard rightly as 'their final destiny'. |

| pónere with no object (*propter dolos posuísti eis*) | pusestes para eles | open | Ps 72:18 (ἔθου αὐτοῖς). Draft 1 supplied DRB's *o*; no reader could place it. Brazilian leaves the object of *pôr* unspoken, so v2 follows the Latin; gate passed. *vós lhes pusestes laços* and MS1932's *prosperidade enganosa* interpret. |

| surgéntes (*sómnium surgéntium*) | os que se levantam | open | Ps 72:20 (ἐξεγειρομένου, one awaking). The ambiguity reader heard 'those who rise up / rebel' as possible; *sonho* beside it points to waking. *despertam* (DRB, MS1932) option. |

| fornicári abs te | prostituir-se longe de vós | open | Ps 72:27 (πορνεύοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ), the prophets' image of idolatry kept; *fornicar* is heard coarse or as a sexual term; MS1932 *infiéis* explains. The ambiguity reader heard literal prostitution first. 105:39 *fornicáti sunt in adinventiónibus suis* decides with it. |

| effúndi (*effúsi sunt gressus mei*) | derramar-se (*quase se derramaram os meus passos*) | open | Ps 72:2 (ἐξεχύθη), the image kept (D42's verb); the ambiguity reader found it puzzling but heard 'nearly failing', the sense. *escorregaram* (DRB) option. |
formulas: | *Quam bonus Israël Deus, rectis corde!* (72:1; Graduals 02-27, 03-27, 06-04 and the Tract of Palm Sunday, Quad6-0, with 72:2–3) · *Tenuísti manum déxteram meam: et in voluntáte tua deduxísti me: et cum glória assumpsísti me* (72:24; Gradual 03-27, Quad6-0) | *Como Deus é bom para Israel, * para os que são retos de coração!* · *Tomastes a minha mão direita: e pela vossa vontade me guiastes, * e com glória me acolhestes* — the Missal's *assumpsísti* would need its own verb | open — Ps 72 |

| *Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in ætérnum* (72:26b; Alleluia 06-04, 10-17; responsory SanctiM Pent02-6b) · *Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est: pónere in Dómino Deo spem meam* (72:28; versicles 05-13, Urbis 07-17, Pent02-6b) | *Deus do meu coração, * e a minha parte é Deus para sempre* · *Mas para mim é bom apegar-me a Deus: * pôr no Senhor Deus a minha esperança* | open — Ps 72; the copula is supplied only in the second member of 72:26b |
